question: If thyroid hormone levels in the blood get very high, what happens to thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) from the pituitary?

options.A: TSH release remains completely unchanged
options.B: TSH release decreases due to negative feedback
options.C: TSH release stops entirely and permanently

question: Why is it helpful for nurses to understand the emotional shifts pregnant women go through?

question: Why is community participation essential in health promotion?

options.A: People must be involved in identifying their own health needs and solutions

question: When assessing a patient who might easily catch infections, what should a nurse check?

question: Why is overfilling a sharps safety box a dangerous hazard?

question: What is the biggest benefit of standardizing nursing workflows on the ward?

options.A: To increase the amount of daily paperwork required
options.B: To make clinical actions predictable and reduce cognitive load
options.C: To eliminate the need for physician orders in emergencies
options.D: To ensure all nurses work the exact same number of hours

explanation: Standardization creates a comforting routine. When tasks are done the same way across the unit, you don't have to overthink every little step, freeing up your brain for patient care! [learn more](GST319_U5_T8#GST319_U5_T8_h4)

question: A toddler comes in with a barking cough and noisy breathing (stridor). What should you, as the nurse, prepare for?

options.A: Prepare equipment for a steam tent
options.B: Administer a dry oxygen mask at high flow
options.C: Apply a cold ice pack to the chest wall

question: When a nurse calls someone to let them know they were exposed to an illness, what must they NOT do?

options.C: Explaining the symptoms to watch out for during the next two weeks

question: How did past pharmaceutical disasters change healthcare rules around the world?

options.A: They caused governments to ban all chemical medications permanently

question: Why must nurses strongly advise patients NEVER to squeeze or pop a vulval cyst at home?

options.C: It will instantly trigger cancerous cell growth

question: Which of these is a very common fall hazard found in many homes?

options.A: Loose scatter rugs on polished floors

question: What is the primary immunological benefit of early colostrum feeding for a newborn?

options.A: Lowering infant red blood cell destruction rates

options.C: Providing high concentrations of secretory IgA antibodies
options.D: Preventing the development of physiological jaundice

explanation: Colostrum is packed with antibodies that coat the baby's digestive tract, protecting them from harmful bacteria and viruses. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T51#GNS214_U1_T51_h6)

question: A mother is scared that immunization injections will make her baby sick. How should you respond?

options.A: Scold her for ignoring professional medical advice

options.C: Advise her to skip the injections entirely if she feels worried

question: What is the main use of a fetal fibronectin test in the hospital?

options.A: To rule out delivery within the next two weeks when negative

options.C: To confirm the exact gestational age in weeks and days

question: What is the single most important action to stop contact infections from spreading in a hospital?

options.A: Administering prophylactic antibiotics to all new admissions
options.B: Wearing sterile surgical masks during visiting hours
options.C: Proper hand hygiene before and after patient contact
options.D: Changing bed linens twice daily for every patient

question: Why do nurses apply an ice pack to the perineum right after a vaginal delivery?

options.B: To reduce localized swelling and numb pain
options.C: To prevent the uterus from becoming boggy

question: Which of these groups is considered a vulnerable population needing extra research protection?

options.A: Licensed physicians
options.B: Children

question: During a sudden storm, a boat nurse needs to assess a patient. What is the most important first step for safety?

options.A: Administer a strong sedative so the patient sleeps through the storm.

options.C: Transport the patient immediately to the captain's private quarters.

question: How do government irrigation projects help boost farming?

options.A: By reducing total dependence on seasonal rainfall for farming
options.B: By lowering the market price of chemical fertilizers
options.C: By giving formal land certificates to rural farmers
options.D: By providing cash loans to farmer groups

explanation: Irrigation gives crops water even during dry seasons, which means farmers can grow food all year round. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T18#GNS214_U1_T18_h2)

question: What makes thyroid hormones act a bit differently than other amino acid-derived hormones?

options.C: They cannot travel in the bloodstream without dissolving in red blood cells
options.D: They are fat-soluble and enter cells to bind intracellular receptors

explanation: Even though they start from an amino acid, thyroid hormones behave like fat-loving steroids—they slip right inside the cell to do their work. Tricky, but you'll never forget it now! [learn more](GNS211_U1_T10#GNS211_U1_T10_h3)

question: A patient asks why walking helps reduce swelling in their legs after surgery. What is the nurse's best response?

options.B: Skeletal muscle contractions squeeze lymph vessels to push fluid upward

question: Why is early initiation of CPR critical during a cardiac arrest?

options.B: It eliminates the need for any medications or defibrillation later

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should do before starting a community health project?

question: Why is a previous classical cesarean section a strong contraindication for home delivery?

question: What are the three core components of the classic epidemiological triangle?

options.A: Vector, Patient, Hospital

options.C: Bacteria, Virus, Fungus
options.D: Agent, Host, Environment

question: Why do the cells on the very outer layer of your skin not have nuclei?

question: Where do Clostridium tetani spores normally live before getting into the body?

question: What is the primary hormonal job of the corpus luteum during the second half of the cycle?

question: What direction does a 'less than' ogive usually take as it moves across the graph?

question: What is a great benefit of building an open safety culture in a healthcare facility?

options.C: Patients stop asking questions about their medications

question: What does a conceptual model usually look like when you see it in a study?

question: What is the main reason midwives and nurses measure fundal height during antenatal checks?

question: How do poor internet and lack of journal access affect local nursing research?

question: What is the main thing that defines an indirect cost?

options.D: It only occurs during night shift operations

question: What is the correct immediate action when a nurse discovers a vital sign monitor has a broken power cord?

question: What is the main purpose of doing a baseline psychiatric assessment for a patient with a degenerative illness?

question: When can palliative care be started for someone with a serious illness?

question: What is the usual maximum safe volume of fluid for one subcutaneous injection in an adult?

question: Which of these is NOT a major challenge to eating a diverse diet in Nigeria?

question: Why do doctors often ask for multiple stool samples when testing for intestinal parasites?

question: A patient asks why she needs extra iron when her test shows mild anemia. What is your best reply?

question: Which of these is an example of biochemical data collected during a nutrition check?

question: Why does a pregnant woman's body absorb nutrients much better?

question: Which of the following is NOT a common cause of disrupted ovarian cycles?

question: Why doesn't having plenty of food in the country automatically mean everyone is well-nourished?

options.A: Government regulations legally restrict citizens from buying more than basic rations

options.C: Stored food spoils instantly before it can be transported to local neighborhood markets
options.D: Food may be present in the country but remain unaffordable or inaccessible to poor households

question: Which position is most commonly used when giving an adult patient an enema?

question: When caring for a client at home, what do psychosocial needs mainly focus on?

options.C: Physical strength and mobility recovery
options.D: Strict adherence to medication timetables

explanation: You're looking at the whole person here! Psychosocial needs are all about feelings, social connections, and mental peace, not just treating a physical illness. Great job keeping this in mind! [learn more](GNS324_U2_T2#GNS324_U2_T2_h1)

question: A patient says they cannot afford the expensive imported supplements prescribed elsewhere. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Report the patient to the hospital management
options.B: Tell the patient to stop eating altogether
options.C: Tell them to borrow money to buy the brand
options.D: Help the patient find affordable local whole-food alternatives

question: What is the safest step for a woman experiencing true obstructed labor in a remote village?

options.A: Perform manual pelvic widening in the community clinic
options.B: Encourage aggressive pushing in a squatting position
options.C: Administer oxytocin drip to speed up contractions
options.D: Arrange immediate emergency transfer for surgical delivery

question: Which symptom strongly tells a nurse to check the throat and voice box (larynx)?

options.A: Persistent hoarseness
options.B: Ringing in the ears
options.C: Stuffiness in the nose
options.D: Blurry vision

explanation: Voice changes that stick around for weeks can point to vocal cord bumps, swelling, or growths, meaning it's time for a closer look. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T2#GNS311_U3_T2_h5)

question: Why must an ADR form include a section listing other medications the patient is taking?

options.A: To prove that the hospital pharmacy is well-stocked with supplies

options.C: To determine which pharmaceutical company made the most profit
options.D: To calculate the total financial cost of the patient's treatment

explanation: Patients often take more than one drug at a time. Listing everything helps us figure out if a bad reaction came from drugs interacting with each other. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T6#GNS215_U2_T6_h4)

question: How do performance appraisals directly help improve patient care?

options.A: By identifying staff strengths and areas needing improvement
options.B: By removing all clinical errors from the hospital setting
options.C: By increasing the number of patients assigned per nurse
options.D: By forcing nurses to work longer shifts without extra pay

explanation: When appraisals highlight what you do brilliantly and where you might need a little extra training, the whole ward benefits and patients receive safer care! [learn more](GST321_U1_T21#GST321_U1_T21_h1)

question: What weather condition in tropical regions like Nigeria contributes greatly to skin fungal infections?

options.A: Frequent consumption of contaminated municipal water supplies
options.B: High environmental humidity and warm weather conditions
options.C: Lack of personal hygiene products in local markets
options.D: Widespread resistance to standard antibacterial vaccines

explanation: You got it! Fungi love warmth and moisture. Our wonderful tropical climate means we see plenty of superficial skin fungal infections in clinical practice. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T3#GNS215_U6_T3_h5)

question: When do we usually rely on indirect sources of data to track maternal mortality?

options.A: When international donors refuse to look at hospital logbooks
options.B: When civil registration systems are incomplete or non-functional
options.C: When every single pregnant woman delivers inside a tertiary clinic
options.D: When hospitals have too much digital data to process manually

explanation: In many areas, births and deaths happen at home and aren't captured by official government books. That's when indirect methods become a lifesaver for getting accurate statistics! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T016#GNS226_U1_T016_h3)

question: Why do poorly ventilated and overcrowded rooms make the spread of TB worse?

options.A: They trap airborne droplet nuclei and keep concentrations high.
options.B: They weaken human skin barriers against germs.
options.C: They lower the room temperature and freeze the bacteria.
options.D: They cause people to share contaminated food items.

explanation: Without fresh air moving in and out, infectious droplets just hang around in the room, making it much easier for someone nearby to breathe them in. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T5#GNS214_U1_T5_h2)

question: Why do symptoms of serum sickness usually take one to three weeks to show up after taking a new medication?

options.A: The liver must slowly break down the medicine into toxic metabolites.
options.B: The medication stays inactive in the stomach for several days before absorbing.
options.C: White blood cells are temporarily paralyzed by the foreign serum.
options.D: It takes time for the body to produce antibodies against the foreign proteins.

explanation: Think of it like a delayed response: your immune system needs a little time to recognize the foreign substance and build up antibodies. [learn more](GST114_U4_T10#GST114_U4_T10_h1)

question: What happens when a hospital fails to accurately calculate the cost of its nursing services?

options.A: Patients receive too many medications
options.B: It struggles to set fair prices and manage budgets
options.C: Doctors refuse to admit new patients
options.D: The hospital building loses structural value

explanation: If you don't know what your services actually cost, it's impossible to set fair prices or keep the hospital financially healthy. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h2)

question: What do we mean by Post-Ebola Syndrome?

options.A: A collection of chronic physical symptoms persisting after recovery
options.B: A permanent mental illness from the incubation period
options.C: An acute respiratory infection before fever starts
options.D: A sudden relapse of active internal bleeding on day two

explanation: You got it! Even after beating the virus, survivors can deal with lingering joint pain, fatigue, and vision issues. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T11#GNS214_U1_T11_h8)

question: What does 'asepsis' mean in your daily nursing practice?

options.A: The complete destruction of all life forms on human skin
options.B: The chemical disinfection of hospital floors and walls
options.C: The total absence of disease-producing microorganisms
options.D: The administration of prophylactic antibiotics before surgery

explanation: Great job! Asepsis simply means keeping an environment or item free from harmful germs that cause infections. You've got this! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h1)

question: How do Standard Precautions differ from original Universal Precautions?

options.A: Standard Precautions remove the need for handwashing if gloves are worn
options.B: Standard Precautions apply to all body fluids and moist tissues, not just blood
options.C: Standard Precautions ignore non-intact skin and focus solely on respiratory droplets
options.D: Standard Precautions are only used when a patient has a confirmed laboratory diagnosis

explanation: While Universal Precautions focused mainly on blood, Standard Precautions broaden the safety net to include all body fluids, secretions, and non-intact skin for every patient. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h1)

question: How were early population control programs different from modern reproductive rights?

options.A: Early programs focused exclusively on treating infertility rather than contraception
options.B: Modern frameworks rely on government-mandated family sizes to reduce poverty
options.C: Modern frameworks ignore maternal health in favor of economic development
options.D: Early programs prioritized national demographic targets over individual bodily autonomy

explanation: In the past, programs often focused on hitting government population numbers. Today, we focus on respecting each person's individual rights and personal choices. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T1#GNS216_U1_T1_h2)

question: What is the main goal of surgical debridement in osteomyelitis?

options.A: To fuse the adjacent joints together permanently
options.B: To stretch the limb to make it longer
options.C: To replace all marrow with synthetic polymers
options.D: To remove dead and infected bone tissue

explanation: Debridement is basically a clean-up operation where the surgeon scrapes away all the dead, infected bone that antibiotics alone can't reach. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T18#GNS222_U1_T18_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a systemic risk associated with unsafe or unnecessary injections?

options.A: Systemic complications from contaminated equipment
options.B: Transmission of Hepatitis B and C viruses
options.C: Development of complete tolerance to oral painkillers
options.D: Acquisition of secondary bloodstream infections

explanation: Unsafe injections cause infections and bloodborne virus transmission, not oral drug tolerance. The question asks for what is NOT a risk. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T6#GNS122_U4_T6_h6)

question: Which of these details must you include when charting AROM exercises?

options.C: The specific joints exercised and the number of repetitions
options.D: The exact cost of the physical therapy equipment

explanation: Good documentation means noting down exactly which joints you worked on and how many times they moved. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T2#GNS221_U1_T2_h7)

question: Which post-WWII law provided funding for hospital construction and indirectly led to the growth of nursing homes?

options.A: The Social Security Amendment
options.B: The Medicare and Medicaid Act
options.C: The Nursing Home Reform Act
options.D: The Hill-Burton Act

question: A newborn delivered after a prolonged labor with severe cephalopelvic disproportion is at the highest risk for which condition?

options.A: Primary pulmonary hypertension

options.D: Foetal skull injury

question: What is an example of a 'forcing function' used to keep patients safe in a hospital?

options.A: Verbally reminding nurses to check blood pressure twice a shift

options.C: Punishing staff members who forget to sign documentation sheets
options.D: Feeding tubes that physically cannot connect to intravenous lines

question: Why do modern nursing units often prefer a flat organizational structure?

options.B: It removes the need for any nurse managers or supervisors
options.C: It guarantees that every patient has a private room
options.D: It completely stops nurses from ever working night shifts

explanation: Exactly! Cutting out too many layers of management helps nurses act faster and talk directly with leaders when patient needs arise. [learn more](GST321_U6_T1#GST321_U6_T1_h2)

question: What is the best mindset for a nurse handling conflict within the healthcare team?

options.A: Viewing conflict as a problem to solve together
options.B: Reporting every minor disagreement to the police
options.C: Ignoring the argument until someone else fixes it
options.D: Proving that the other person is completely wrong

explanation: You got it! Tackling disagreements as a team issue rather than a personal fight helps everyone reach a peaceful, patient-centered solution. [learn more](GST321_U7_T2#GST321_U7_T2_h7)

question: What is a key role of water as a solvent in the human body?

options.D: It allows cellular chemical reactions to take place.

question: What is the best way to prevent opioid-induced constipation in palliative patients?

question: What is the main point of using motivational interviewing during nutrition counseling?

options.C: Speeding up the clinical consultation to save hospital time
options.D: Helping patients resolve their ambivalence about changing eating habits

question: How can a home health nurse practice primary prevention during routine visits?

question: Why would a nurse choose the intradermal route for giving a medication?

question: What protective gear is a must when handling strong, concentrated chemical disinfectants?

question: Which of the following is a non-pharmacological method for managing physical discomfort?

question: What actually happens during a pelvic organ prolapse?

question: Through which part of the spinal cord do incoming sensory nerve signals enter?

question: What does a lab tech look at during a macroscopic check of a culture plate?

question: A school clinic notices a sudden jump in waterborne infections among students. What should the team do next?

question: Which bacterium is responsible for the majority of bone infection cases?

question: What is the ultimate goal when you empower a patient through nutrition counselling?

options.D: Patient independence in making healthy food choices

question: Which sign might tell you that a patient is struggling during a ventilator weaning trial?

question: What usually happens right in the initial moments after a clinical error occurs?

options.D: Immediate filing of retirement paperwork

explanation: In those first scary moments, you're usually in shock while frantically trying to stabilize the patient. Your clinical survival instincts kick right in! [learn more](GST319_U6_T4#GST319_U6_T4_h3)

question: How often should a bedbound patient usually be turned to prevent bedsores?

options.B: Every two hours

options.D: Only when they complain of pain

question: In the ward, what do we call a non-living object—like a BP cuff or a table—that can transfer germs?

options.B: A type of protective mask worn during surgery

question: Which stomach cells are responsible for secreting hydrochloric acid?

question: Your patient just took a sip of water and now sounds wet and gurgling when they speak. What is your very first nursing move?

question: When health systems face a 'double burden of disease', what two types of health challenges are they dealing with?

options.B: Acute poisoning and chronic malnutrition

question: What is the main job of the pudendal nerve during ejaculation?

question: How do we mostly define a "community" in public health nursing?

question: Which simple nursing action helps relax tummy muscles and ease pain for a patient having severe cramps (colic)?

question: Why is the biopsychosocial model especially useful in psychiatric nursing?

options.C: It replaces the need for any laboratory testing or physical exams
options.D: It proves that all mental illnesses are caused by bad parenting

explanation: Because mental disorders have multiple roots, this model encourages nurses to assess physical, emotional, and social aspects of a patient's life for holistic care. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T4#GNS314_U2_T4_h1)

question: Which tiny structures in the upper dermis are responsible for giving you your unique fingerprints?

question: Which layer of the skin acts as the main shield blocking most drugs from easily entering the body?

question: Which group of foods gives us complete proteins packed with all the amino acids our bodies need?

question: Why is washing hands with soap and water so important before a home blood glucose test?

question: Before opening a standard catheter kit, which major allergies must you always check for?

question: Which type of vaccine uses a weakened (but still alive) version of a germ?

question: Why should a surgical knot be positioned to the side of the wound incision rather than directly over it?

question: What do we call a child who is academically gifted but also has a learning disability?

question: What is the main job of a mechanical ventilator when a patient cannot breathe well on their own?

question: Why must healthcare workers share disease outbreak data quickly with sanitation departments?

question: Why do we place a waterproof sheet on an operation (surgical) bed?

question: How does promising strict privacy change how teenagers use reproductive health services?

question: What should a nurse do if a low-risk pregnant woman develops severe anemia during her third trimester?

question: Why must you let the skin antiseptic dry completely before starting an IV stick?

question: How often should you check a stable newborn's vital signs right after birth?

question: What is the best way for a nurse to find out about hidden food taboos during a patient assessment?

question: When is a stool culture typically ordered for a patient with gastroenteritis?

question: What does cultural competence mainly ask of a home health nurse?

question: A rural clinic notices a weekly increase in watery diarrhea during the rainy season. What should the nurses do first?

question: Why do pregnant women routinely get screened for STIs during early prenatal visits?

options.D: Vitamin B12

explanation: Pyridoxine, or Vitamin B6, is widely recommended as a safe and effective starting medication for pregnancy nausea. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T012#GNS226_U2_T012_h5)

question: A toddler with diarrhoea drinks eagerly from a cup and seems restless. How would you grade this?

options.A: Severe dehydration
options.B: No dehydration
options.C: Some dehydration
options.D: Chronic dehydration

explanation: Spot on! When a child drinks eagerly and is a bit restless or irritable, it's a classic sign of moderate ('some') dehydration. They are thirsty and ready for ORS! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T56#GNS214_U1_T56_h3)

question: In nursing, what does the common acronym ADL stand for?

options.A: Advanced Dietary List
options.B: Alternate Drug Logistics
options.C: Activities of Daily Living
options.D: Acute Disease Level

explanation: You nailed it! ADLs are the everyday things we do to care for ourselves, like bathing, dressing, and eating. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T2#GNS324_U5_T2_h3)

question: Which nerve is most at risk when a gluteal (buttock) injection is given with poor technique?

options.A: Femoral nerve
options.B: Median nerve
options.C: Sciatic nerve
options.D: Radial nerve

explanation: Great nursing knowledge! The sciatic nerve runs deep in the lower buttock, so injections must be placed carefully in the upper outer quadrant to avoid it. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h5)

question: What physical change directly leads to a loss of independence in degenerative muscle disorders?

options.A: Sudden increases in bone density
options.B: Rapid regeneration of nerve tissues
options.C: Permanent high blood pressure
options.D: Progressive muscle wasting and weakness

explanation: As muscle fibers waste away and weaken, patients gradually lose the physical strength needed to move and care for themselves. You've got this! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T17#GNS222_U4_T17_h2)

question: What must be done to heat-sensitive instruments after they undergo chemical cold sterilization?

options.A: Store them immediately inside a sealed plastic bag
options.B: Wipe them dry with an ordinary cloth towel
options.C: Rinse them thoroughly using sterile water
options.D: Heat them briefly over an open spirit flame

explanation: Chemical sterilants are toxic to human tissue and must be washed off with sterile water to prevent chemical burns or irritation. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h3)

question: What causes the nutritional paradox where a person is both overweight and undernourished?

options.A: Eating many cheap calories that lack essential micronutrients
options.B: Absorbing too many vitamins from cheap processed snacks
options.C: Consuming too much pure water alongside sugary drinks
options.D: Exercising too much while eating high-protein diets

explanation: When people fill up on cheap, heavy foods, they get plenty of energy (calories) but miss out on crucial vitamins and minerals. Great job thinking this through! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T020#GNS227_U2_T020_h2)

question: What makes hot and cold packs such great choices in everyday nursing care?

options.A: They prevent all forms of skin breakdown automatically
options.B: They completely eliminate the need for physician supervision
options.C: They work instantly to heal surgical incisions overnight
options.D: They offer a cost-effective way to help manage pain without medication

explanation: Exactly! They are affordable, readily available, and give patients that extra touch of relief alongside their regular medications. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T8#GNS221_U3_T8_h1)

question: Which of these is a big NO-WHEN managing medical waste during a home visit?

options.A: Following local health regulations for biological waste disposal
options.B: Using a puncture-proof plastic container for used lancets
options.C: Throwing used bloody gauze into the household kitchen trash
options.D: Placing infectious waste bags in designated community drop-offs

explanation: Correct! Bloody dressings carry pathogens and must never be tossed into regular household rubbish where family members could touch them. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T9#GNS324_U6_T9_h5)

question: What is a community health nurse's main job during early disease surveillance?

options.A: Detecting and reporting unusual symptom clusters
options.B: Declaring a national state of emergency
options.C: Manufacturing vaccines for the community
options.D: Treating severe cases in intensive care units

explanation: You're doing great! Nurses act as our frontline watchdogs by spotting unusual health patterns early and reporting them. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T89#GNS214_U1_T89_h5)

question: What is the single most important and effective step when trying to resuscitate a newborn?

options.A: Giving emergency IV drugs
options.B: Ventilating the newborn's lungs with air or oxygen
options.C: Giving a quick fluid drip
options.D: Doing chest compressions

explanation: Most newborn emergencies happen because they aren't breathing. Getting oxygen into their lungs is always our top rescue step! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T011#GNS226_U1_T011_h3)

question: Why are very premature babies with low birth weight at a higher risk of developing cerebral palsy?

options.A: Fragile blood vessels in the immature brain easily rupture and bleed
options.B: Premature babies automatically have defective muscle tissue from birth
options.C: The lungs fail to develop, which immediately starves the heart of oxygen
options.D: Infant formulas lack the essential fats required for nerve growth

explanation: Preterm babies have very delicate blood vessels in their brains that can easily bleed, which can damage the surrounding brain tissue. Great insight for your clinical postings! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T4#GNS324_U4_T4_h2)

question: As a nurse, what is your most important duty when caring for an elderly patient with severe osteoporosis?

options.A: Applying continuous heavy traction to strengthen weak leg bones
options.B: Restricting dietary calcium intake to prevent mineral crystal buildup
options.C: Implementing strict fall prevention protocols in the environment
options.D: Encouraging complete bed rest to prevent accidental bone trauma

explanation: Prevention is key! Keeping the environment safe from slips and trips protects fragile bones from breaking. Excellent nursing care! [learn more](GNS121_U3_T4#GNS121_U3_T4_h8)

question: What is a main goal of couples counseling when treating female sexual dysfunction?

options.A: Legally binding the couple to a specific treatment plan
options.B: Improving communication and reducing performance anxiety
options.C: Performing physical examinations on both partners together
options.D: Prescribing precise hormonal dosages for the female partner

explanation: You're doing great! Counseling helps partners talk openly, take off the pressure of strict expectations, and grow closer together. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T25#GNS312_U1_T25_h8)

question: Which digital tool is commonly used to send quick appointment reminders straight to a pregnant client's phone?

options.A: SMS text messages
options.B: Megaphone broadcasts
options.C: Flannel graphs
options.D: Printed paper posters

explanation: Simple SMS text messages land directly on personal phones, making them a super convenient way to remind clients not to miss their antenatal visits. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T5#GNS124_U5_T5_h5)

question: Student nurses are preparing an outreach during the rainy season when cholera is common. What should they bring?

options.A: Bring water purification and cholera prevention flipcharts to demonstrate safe drinking habits
options.B: Leave all educational materials behind and only administer treatments quietly
options.C: Focus the entire talk on newborn baby care and breastfeeding techniques
options.D: Bring posters about snakebite prevention exclusively because they are colorful

explanation: Matching your materials to seasonal threats like cholera means your outreach hits right where help is needed most! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T4#GNS124_U5_T4_h7)

question: Why do patients with heart valve problems often develop a heart murmur?

options.A: The electrical wires in the heart rub against each other.
options.B: Turbulent blood flow occurs as blood moves through narrowed or leaky valves.
options.C: Air gets trapped inside the heart muscle tissue.
options.D: The lungs make whistling sounds during deep breathing.

explanation: Normally, blood flows smoothly and quietly. But when it's forced through a tight or leaky valve, it splashes around and makes a WHOOSH sound—which we call a murmur! [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a sign of low calcium levels in the blood?

options.A: Nerve twitching and muscle spasms
options.B: Increased neuromuscular irritability
options.C: Numbness around the mouth
options.D: Increased muscle strength and bulk

explanation: You got it! Low calcium makes nerves super jumpy (causing tingles and spasms), but it doesn't magically build bigger muscles. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T7#GNS123_U3_T7_h5)

question: Why do nurses monitor hourly urine output so closely when caring for a patient in shock?

options.A: It prevents the urinary bladder from overstretching during fluid resuscitation
options.B: It confirms whether the patient has a urinary tract infection
options.C: It is a reliable indicator of renal perfusion and overall organ blood flow
options.D: It directly measures the current blood glucose levels in the bloodstream

explanation: Your kidneys are like little warning lights. If they aren't making urine, it tells you they aren't getting enough blood flow—which means other vital organs are likely suffering too. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T3#GNS112_U7_T3_h4)

question: What problem do instructional materials help reduce by giving students a concrete picture of a concept?

options.A: Verbalism
options.B: Dehydration
options.C: Hypertension
options.D: Somnolence

explanation: Verbalism happens when students use or hear words without truly understanding what they mean, which teaching aids prevent by showing the actual object or process. [learn more](GST321_U8_T4#GST321_U8_T4_h2)

question: Why would a nurse place the bell of a stethoscope over an enlarged thyroid gland?

options.A: To listen for a bruit caused by increased blood flow
options.B: To check for crackles moving up from the trachea
options.C: To measure the exact width of the thyroid lobes
options.D: To assess for abnormal whistling breath sounds

explanation: An overactive thyroid sucks up a massive amount of blood. That rushing blood creates an audible whooshing sound called a bruit that you can actually hear through your stethoscope! [learn more](GNS222_U2_T3#GNS222_U2_T3_h4)

question: What is another common medical name for hydatid disease?

options.A: Taeniasis
options.B: Schistosomiasis
options.C: Ascariasis
options.D: Echinococcosis

explanation: Hydatid disease comes from tapeworm larvae and is medically called echinococcosis. You've got this! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T25#GNS313_U2_T25_h1)

question: What happens to the pelvic floor as the uterus grows heavier in the third trimester?

options.A: It pulls the pelvic floor upward to relieve stress on the bladder
options.B: It has no mechanical impact until actual labor begins
options.C: It places constant downward pressure that stretches the muscle fibers
options.D: It strengthens the muscles by forcing them to contract continuously

explanation: Well done! Gravity and a growing baby mean continuous downward pressure, which can stretch and tire out these hardworking muscles over time. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T12#GNS121_U5_T12_h2)

question: A nurse teaches primary school pupils about handwashing. Six weeks later, she checks if the rate of diarrhea among the children has dropped. What type of evaluation is this?

options.A: Financial budgeting
options.B: Impact evaluation
options.C: Logistical planning
options.D: Baseline assessment

explanation: Spot on! Looking at long-term health changes—like a drop in illness rates—tells you the real impact your teaching made. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T1#GNS214_U1_T1_h7)

question: If a patient has a stroke on the right side of their motor cortex, which side of the body will show physical weakness?

options.A: The right side
options.B: The left side
options.C: Only the lower limbs
options.D: Both sides equally

explanation: Brilliant! Brain pathways cross over in the brainstem, so damage on the right side of the brain shows up as weakness on the left side of the body. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T12#GNS222_U3_T12_h4)

question: What is the usual daily fat limit for a strict low-fat therapeutic diet?

options.A: Exactly zero grams per day
options.B: Less than 20 grams per day
options.C: Around 70 to 100 grams daily
options.D: Up to 50 percent of total calories

explanation: You got this! A strict low-fat diet keeps fat under 20 grams daily. Eating completely zero fat is almost impossible with natural foods. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T006#GNS227_U6_T006_h1)

question: What is the simple difference between responsibility and accountability?

options.A: Responsibility requires no supervision, while accountability requires reporting
options.B: Responsibility applies only to doctors, while accountability applies to nurses
options.C: Responsibility is doing the task, while accountability is answering for the outcome
options.D: Responsibility is a legal term, while accountability is purely moral

explanation: You can be given the job to do (responsibility), but accountability means you answer for how it all turns out. You've got this! [learn more](GST321_U1_T17#GST321_U1_T17_h2)

question: Which of these is an example of a macronutrient that the body needs in large amounts?

options.A: Trace minerals
options.B: Iron supplements
options.C: Vitamins
options.D: Carbohydrates

explanation: Correct! 'Macro' means big—carbs, proteins, and fats are the big-ticket items our bodies need daily in large quantities for fuel. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T007#GNS227_U1_T007_h4)

question: What exactly is a community health risk?

options.A: The total cost of running a primary health care clinic
options.B: Any factor increasing the chance of illness or injury for a group
options.C: A personal medical diagnosis given inside a hospital ward
options.D: A genetic disease passed down through generations in a family

explanation: Think of community health risks as collective dangers that affect many people together, rather than just one person's isolated sickness. You've got this! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T9#GNS122_U3_T9_h1)

question: Why do we use an interdisciplinary team in palliative care?

options.A: It reduces the total number of staff members needed in a hospital
options.B: It covers the diverse physical, emotional, and spiritual needs of the patient
options.C: It prevents families from speaking with the healthcare team
options.D: It ensures that doctors make all decisions without consulting others

explanation: Fantastic! Because end-of-life care touches every part of a person's life, it takes a diverse team of experts to cover all their physical, emotional, and spiritual needs. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T3#GNS321_U4_T3_h7)

question: Why is asking about the last menstrual period crucial during an emergency contraception assessment?

options.C: To determine how much weight the patient has recently gained

question: What happens during qualitative data analysis?

options.C: Researchers code text to identify recurring themes and patterns
options.D: Blood samples are centrifuged in a hospital laboratory

explanation: Qualitative analysis organizes narrative words and interviews into meaningful categories or themes. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T1#GNS217_U3_T1_h6)

question: If you want to share health news quickly in a village, what should you look for first?

options.A: Written laws governing foreign healthcare workers
options.B: Local communication networks and gathering places
options.C: The distance to the nearest major city
options.D: The exact number of brick houses in the area

question: Which hormone helps your body handle long-term stress?

options.A: Melatonin
options.B: Insulin
options.C: Cortisol
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: You nailed it! Cortisol is your body's main stress manager, helping you cope with physical and emotional pressure over time. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T1#GNS211_U1_T1_h4)

question: Which of these actions with a used sharps box is dangerous and completely wrong?

question: Why does milk production stop when a baby is abruptly weaned?

options.A: The posterior pituitary gland permanently stops producing oxytocin stores.

options.C: Accumulated milk triggers feedback inhibitors that signal secretory cells to halt production.

question: What is the primary danger of leaving a needle stuck in a multidose vaccine vial?

options.A: It changes the recommended dosage for pediatric clients

options.C: It causes the liquid vaccine to freeze too quickly

question: A young female patient asks how she got a fallopian tube infection when she felt fine down below. What is the most likely reason?

options.A: A sudden genetic mutation in her uterine lining cells
options.B: An asymptomatic ascending sexually transmitted infection like chlamydia
options.C: A severe allergic reaction to standard hormonal contraceptives

question: What is the most important fluid instruction to give a patient taking an expectorant?

options.C: Restrict all fluids for two hours before and after taking the pill

question: A patient arrives at the ward with a stab wound to the chest and difficulty breathing. What condition should you suspect?

options.A: Severe bacterial pneumonia

options.C: Pneumothorax or hemothorax
options.D: Pulmonary edema from heart failure

question: What is the main goal of palliative care?

options.A: To shorten the dying process
options.B: To replace family caregiving
options.C: To cure terminal illnesses
options.D: To improve quality of life

explanation: Palliative care focuses primarily on relieving symptoms and stress to give the patient and family the best possible quality of life. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T11#GNS321_U4_T11_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of epidemiological surveillance in public health?

options.A: Punishing healthcare facilities that fail to report sick patients
options.B: Providing free prescription medications to rural communities
options.C: Conducting laboratory research on new pharmaceutical drugs
options.D: Continuous collection and analysis of health data to guide action

explanation: Great job! Surveillance simply means keeping a close, ongoing eye on disease numbers so health workers can spot trouble early and act fast. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T13#GNS313_U1_T13_h5)

question: Which group of workers faces the highest daily risk of exposure to bloodborne infections like HIV and Hepatitis B?

options.A: Healthcare workers
options.B: Textile factory weavers
options.C: Road construction workers
options.D: Office administrative staff

explanation: Because we frequently handle needles, sharps, and patient body fluids, healthcare personnel face a higher risk of bloodborne infections. Safety first! [learn more](GNS225_U7_T5#GNS225_U7_T5_h4)

question: Which tiny flap of tissue stops food from accidentally entering your windpipe (trachea) when you swallow?

options.A: The vocal cords
options.B: The lower esophageal sphincter
options.C: The epiglottis
options.D: The soft palate

explanation: The epiglottis is like a clever trapdoor. It folds down over your larynx every time you swallow to make sure food safely slips into your esophagus instead of your lungs. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T011#GNS227_U1_T011_h3)

question: What do we call non-living things like bed sheets, instruments, or toys that carry germs to a patient?

options.A: Zoonoses
options.B: Carriers
options.C: Vectors
options.D: Fomites

explanation: Fomites are everyday objects (like stethoscope tubes or door handles) that pick up germs and pass them along. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T5#GNS313_U1_T5_h6)

question: If a hospital ward wants the most accurate count of surgical infections, which method should they use?

options.A: Patient self-reporting through comment cards left in the waiting room
options.B: Annual surveys sent out to former patients via postal mail six months later
options.C: Passive surveillance by waiting for surgeons to submit written feedback forms
options.D: Active surveillance by reviewing lab results and patient charts directly

explanation: Well done! Proactively checking charts and lab results catches infections that busy doctors and nurses might miss through normal reporting. [learn more](GST114_U2_T22#GST114_U2_T22_h3)

question: What is the main goal of adding social inclusion into nursing care plans?

options.A: To ensure that all hospital beds are filled by patients from identical backgrounds
options.B: To eliminate the need for physicians to write formal medical prescriptions
options.C: To empower vulnerable patients and reduce health disparities caused by social inequality
options.D: To force patients to change their cultural and religious beliefs before discharge

explanation: Social inclusion in nursing is all about making sure everyone gets fair, respectful care by tackling the root causes of discrimination and helping patients speak for themselves. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T5#GNS312_U4_T5_h7)

question: What is an urban 'food desert'?

options.A: A farming community that refuses to grow crops
options.B: A dry region where no humans live
options.C: An area lacking affordable and fresh whole foods
options.D: A marketplace that sells only drinking water

explanation: Food deserts are city neighborhoods where residents struggle to easily find and buy fresh, healthy food options. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T022#GNS227_U2_T022_h5)

question: Which of the following complications is strongly linked to poor nutritional status in bedridden patients?

options.A: Ear infections
options.B: Kidney stones
options.C: Vision loss
options.D: Pressure injuries

explanation: Malnourished tissue breaks down much faster under pressure, making pressure injuries very common in vulnerable patients. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T001#GNS227_U5_T001_h5)

question: Which cranial nerve carries taste messages from the front two-thirds of the tongue?

options.B: Vagus nerve (CN X)
options.C: Glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX)
options.D: Facial nerve (CN VII)

question: What can happen if naloxone is pushed too fast into a patient who has been using opioids for a long time?

options.A: A sudden drop in heart rate leading to cardiac arrest
options.B: Immediate kidney failure and permanent anuria
options.C: Permanent paralysis of the skeletal muscles
options.D: Sudden and severe withdrawal symptoms like vomiting and agitation

question: Why are offline hobbies and sports so effective in preventing phone addiction?

options.A: It completely destroys the internal components of digital devices
options.B: It provides alternative sources of fulfillment and reduces reliance on virtual rewards
options.C: It prevents the eyes from ever blinking during daylight hours
options.D: It ensures the teenager never learns how to use modern computers

explanation: Real-world fun like sports, art, or hanging out with friends gives the brain natural satisfaction and connection, making us less glued to our phones. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T14#GNS312_U3_T14_h6)

question: What is the key difference between monitoring and evaluation?

options.A: Monitoring is done only by doctors, while evaluation is done strictly by patients
options.B: Monitoring happens after the project closes, while evaluation happens before it starts
options.C: Monitoring looks at financial costs, whereas evaluation only looks at weather patterns
options.D: Monitoring is ongoing during the project, while evaluation is a formal assessment of results

question: What happens legally to a nurse who performs FGM in countries with strict anti-FGM laws?

options.A: They must pay a small fine for using hospital supplies
options.B: They are reassigned to administrative duties without penalty
options.C: They can face imprisonment and lose their nursing license
options.D: They receive a simple warning from the local health board

question: Which long-term health risk is strongly linked to low oestrogen levels when amenorrhoea is left untreated?

options.A: Chronic kidney failure
options.B: Obstructive sleep apnea
options.C: Type 1 diabetes mellitus
options.D: Osteoporosis

question: Why is it important to educate family members about natural nutritional decline at the end of life?

options.C: To train them to insert feeding tubes at home

question: What is one of the primary frontline duties of a community health nurse during an outbreak?

options.A: Manufacturing vaccines in a laboratory setting

options.C: Tracing contacts and listing exposed individuals
options.D: Writing national health legislation and edicts

question: Why is community education and reducing stigma such a vital part of nursing care for immune conditions?

options.A: It encourages people to seek testing and treatment early without fear.

options.C: It replaces the need for nutritional supplements in rural areas.
options.D: It lowers the cost of manufacturing hospital equipment.

question: What separates a 'child of the street' from other street-connected youth?

options.D: They live in state orphanages but visit the market daily

question: Why does Primary Health Care place such a strong focus on community participation?

options.B: Because the government lacks any funding to pay healthcare workers
options.C: Because international laws forbid centralized hospital construction
options.D: Because programs are more successful and sustainable when locals help plan them

explanation: Exactly! When the community is involved from the start, health projects address real local needs and are warmly accepted. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T7#GNS225_U2_T7_h4)

question: How does tele-nursing change the way we deliver healthcare?
